title: Guardrail simulator for tier-aware routing policies
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Refactor the policy engine's validation surface and add a guardrail simulator that executes routing rules against recorded and synthetic traffic. The goal is to detect unsafe configurations early (region starvation, infinite fallback loops, tier bleed-through, incompatible fallback model variants) and to provide actionable validation errors and remediation suggestions. This work combines a stricter typed-DSL validator with a runtime simulator that models capacity, regional latencies, and variant compatibility so that policy authors can get high-fidelity preflight feedback before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Validator rejects configs with unknown keys and emits schema-precise errors (path + suggestion).
Typed AST must be produced for every policy and used by both the static validator and simulator.
Simulator can run a policy against a 24-hour production trace slice and surface top 10 risky outcomes (region overload, unavailable fallback, model-compat mismatch).
CI gate: PRs that touch policy schemas run the simulator on a small trace and must pass automated checks or explicitly acknowledge risk.
Backward compatibility: existing routing contracts are honored under the migration toggle; when toggle is off the system continues to accept legacy configs.
technical_notes: Introduce a minimal typed-DSL IR (policy AST) that separates semantics (region/tier/fallback) from surface syntax to enable staged migration.
Schema versioning: policy schema v2 with migration adapters that emit deprecation warnings for legacy fields.
Simulator models: region capacity (tokens/sec), tier latency distributions, and model_variant compatibility matrix encoded as cluster metadata.
Use property-based fuzzing (quickcheck-style) to surface pathological rules (e.g., cycles, contradictory constraints).
Add a bounded model-checking pass for loop detection and a cost-estimator to predict token routing cost under SLOs.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add typed AST generation and a permissive validator that annotates issues but does not block (feature flag: policy-ast).
Phase 2: Launch simulator as a preflight check in staging; run against historical traces for high-traffic customers (opt-in beta).
Phase 3: Enable stricter schema enforcement behind an opt-out window and provide an automated migration helper CLI that rewrites deprecated fields.
Phase 4: Flip blocking validation on for new policies and keep a read-only compatibility mode for legacy deployments for 3 months.
tests_and_tools: Unit: schema roundtrip tests and AST invariants.
Integration: simulator end-to-end with synthetic regional capacity profiles.
Regression corpus: collected problematic policies from production incidents (anonymized) used as golden cases.
CI: add 'policy-sim' job that runs fast simulator with 1M synthetic requests budget and fails on >5% risky outcomes.
Dev tooling: local 'policy-lint --simulate' command that emits human-readable runbook suggestions.
